anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Database Memory Allocation Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly : Cardinality and cost inputs fed to the optimizer are stale, incomplete, or misleading, systematically skewing plan selection away from what the actual data distribution would require.
Database Memory Allocation Anomaly : The database engine allocates or retains more memory than the host can supply, resulting in sustained memory pressure, paging, and frequent work-area spills.

When both anomalies manifest simultaneously, the workload exhibits compounded symptoms: queries whose row-count estimates are far below reality may choose memory-hungry hash joins or large in-memory sorts that instantly overrun the already stressed memory envelope; conversely, gross over-estimates may inflate work-area reservations, accelerating buffer-cache eviction and swap activity. Operators that spill to disk because memory is exhausted can generate long execution times, burst I/O, and additional temp-space consumption, while concurrent sessions experience erratic performance and higher CPU wait-for-memory stalls. Monitoring shows a mix of extreme estimate-vs-actual divergences, rapid growth of per-query memory allocations, resident-set inflation, and frequent re-optimization or cursor reloading as memory pressure forces plan cache purges.

Causal interaction: stale or absent statistics mislead the optimizer into selecting plans whose memory footprint is either unintentionally huge or cannot be honored under current load. Those oversized allocations accelerate the memory-allocation anomaly, pushing the engine into aggressive paging or global memory pressure states. In turn, memory pressure triggers more spills and longer runtimes, delaying or canceling automatic statistics refresh jobs and keeping statistics stale, thereby reinforcing the optimizer error. The feedback loop magnifies both root causes, degrading throughput and threatening node stability across OLTP and analytical workloads alike.

entry.official_definition: The time limit for regular expression matching operations performed by the regular expression engine.
entry.trigger_condition: A regular expression match operation exceeds regexp_time_limit.
entry.workload_impact: The regular expression operation is constrained by the configured time limit.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when statement execution exceeds a configured execution-time budget because the operation runs too long or the workload is blocked behind other work.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect query shape, access path quality, resource contention, and whether the timeout threshold should be reviewed together with the workload pattern.
